editorial:
Imagine you are caught between your job and your own child during a time of war. You follow Yacov, a talented architect in 1999, who gets a huge job to build a memorial for fallen soldiers in Lebanon. The problem is his son, Amnon, who thinks the monument should honor everyone who died in the war, not just one side. It is a heavy story about family fights and political tension, but it feels very grounded and real. You will feel the stress between the father and son as they argue over what it actually means to remember the dead.

The acting is the best part here because the tension between the lead actors feels totally natural. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff at the end makes it worth your time. If you enjoy dramas that make you think about right and wrong, you should definitely check this out. Since the scenery is so beautiful, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the details. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for the high quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Yacov decides to change his design to include a space for all victims, finally listening to his son. This choice causes a huge fight with the government, but it heals his relationship with Amnon. The movie wraps up with the monument being finished. You see a shot of people from both sides standing together in silence, showing that peace is possible when you acknowledge everyone's pain.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep family stories and historical dramas.
